name: St. John Chrysostom
title: Archbishop of Constantinople
bio: Renowned preacher and Archbishop of Constantinople, celebrated for his eloquence and his liturgy still used in the Orthodox Church today.

name: St. George
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for his Christian faith, venerated across the Orthodox world as a symbol of courage and the slayer of the dragon.

name: St. Mary of Egypt
title: Venerable
bio: A former sinner who repented and lived decades alone in the desert beyond the Jordan, becoming a model of repentance and asceticism.

locations.label: Desert of repentance — beyond the Jordan

name: St. Gregory Palamas
title: Archbishop of Thessalonica
bio: A monk of Mount Athos and later Archbishop of Thessalonica, he defended the hesychast practice of contemplative prayer against the rationalist Barlaam of Calabria, teaching that God's uncreated energies can truly be experienced by the faithful.

name: St. Nectarios of Aegina
title: Metropolitan of Pentapolis, Wonderworker
bio: Born Anastasios Cephalas, he served as Metropolitan of Pentapolis before being unjustly removed from his post; he later founded Holy Trinity Monastery on Aegina, where he spent his final years and is remembered for many posthumous healing miracles.

name: St. Spyridon of Trimythous
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A simple Cypriot shepherd who became Bishop of Trimythous and attended the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, where he famously explained the Holy Trinity using a piece of brick; his incorrupt relics are now venerated in Corfu, of which he is patron saint.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Trimythous, Cyprus

name: St. Dionysios of Zakynthos
title: Archbishop, Venerable
bio: Born Draganigos Sigouros, he became a monk and later Archbishop of Aegina before retiring to a monastery on his native Zakynthos; he is remembered above all for forgiving the man who, unknowingly, had killed his own brother.

locations.label: Birthplace, monastic life, and relics — Zakynthos

name: St. Cosmas of Aetolia
title: Hieromartyr, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A monk of Mount Athos who spent 25 years traveling on foot throughout Greece and Albania, founding over 200 schools and preaching to villagers left without churches or priests after centuries of Ottoman rule, before being martyred on charges brought against him.

name: St. Basil the Great
title: Archbishop of Caesarea, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia and a leading 4th-century theologian, he defended Orthodoxy against Arianism and founded the Basiliad, a combined poorhouse, hospital, and hostel for the destitute outside his city.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and death — Caesarea, Cappadocia

name: St. Gregory the Theologian
title: Archbishop of Constantinople, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: A close friend of St. Basil the Great, he was chosen Archbishop of Constantinople by the Second Ecumenical Council for his defense of the Trinity against Arianism, before retiring to Nazianzus for the rest of his life.

name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
title: Great Martyr
bio: A learned and noble young woman of Alexandria who confounded fifty pagan philosophers sent to refute her Christian faith and was martyred under Emperor Maximinus; her relics were later found at the monastery bearing her name on Mount Sinai.

name: St. Panteleimon
title: Great Martyr, Unmercenary Healer
bio: A physician of Nicomedia who treated the poor and sick without charge in the name of Christ, he was martyred under Emperor Maximian after healing a paralyzed man before the emperor's own eyes; he is invoked among the unmercenary healer-saints.

name: St. Anthony the Great
title: Venerable, Father of Monasticism
bio: Born to a wealthy family in Egypt, he sold his possessions to follow Christ's call to the poor and withdrew into the desert, becoming the leader of the Desert Fathers and the model for all later Christian monasticism.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Eastern Desert, Egypt

name: St. Sabbas the Sanctified
title: Venerable
bio: A Cappadocian monastic who settled in the Judean desert and founded the Great Lavra (Mar Saba), composing the Jerusalem Typikon that shaped monastic and liturgical practice across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Mar Saba, Judean Desert

name: St. Demetrius of Thessaloniki
title: Great Martyr, Myrrh-streamer
bio: A high-ranking Christian official martyred under Emperor Galerius, he is venerated as the patron and protector of Thessaloniki, where a miraculous flow of fragrant myrrh was later found at his tomb.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom and relics — Thessaloniki

name: St. Paisios of Mount Athos
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: Born Arsenios Eznepidis, his family fled Asia Minor for Greece in his infancy; he became a monk of Mount Athos known for his gentle counsel to the thousands of pilgrims who sought him out, and was canonized in 2015.

locations.label: Death and relics — Souroti, near Thessaloniki

name: St. Gerasimos of Kephalonia
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: Born to a noble Byzantine family, he lived as a hermit on Mount Athos, in Jerusalem, Sinai, Egypt, Crete, and Zakynthos before settling in a cave in Kephalonia, where he restored a church and founded a convent; he is now the island's patron saint.

name: St. Nicholas of Myra
title: Archbishop of Myra, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Myra in Lycia and participant in the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, he is venerated throughout the world for his generosity to the poor and his protection of sailors, children, and the falsely accused. His relics were translated to Bari, Italy in 1087.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Myra (Demre), Lycia

name: St. John the Baptist
title: Prophet, Forerunner, Baptist
bio: The last of the Old Testament prophets and Forerunner of Christ, he proclaimed repentance in the Judean desert, baptized Jesus in the Jordan, and was martyred by Herod Antipas at the request of Salome. He holds the unique liturgical title “Greater than the prophets.”

locations.label: Baptism of Christ — Qasr al-Yahud, Jordan River

name: St. Athanasios the Great
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who championed Nicene orthodoxy against Arianism throughout his life, enduring five exiles at the hands of Arian emperors. His phrase “Athanasios contra mundum” captures his solitary defense of the full divinity of Christ.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and relics — Alexandria

name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who presided over the Third Ecumenical Council of Ephesus (431 AD), which confirmed the title Theotokos (“God-bearer”) for the Virgin Mary against the teaching of Nestorius. His prolific theological writings earned him the title “Seal of the Fathers.”

name: St. Makarios of Egypt
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A disciple of St. Anthony the Great who settled in the Scetis desert of Egypt and became one of the most celebrated Desert Fathers, attracting thousands of monks to the Wadi Natrun. He is the reputed author of the Fifty Spiritual Homilies on the life of inner prayer.

locations.label: Monastic life and relics — Wadi el-Natrun (Scetis)

name: St. Seraphim of Sarov
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: A monk of Sarov in Russia who spent years in hermitage and later opened his cell to thousands of pilgrims, greeting each with the words “My joy!” He taught that the aim of the Christian life is the acquisition of the Holy Spirit, and remains one of the most beloved saints of the Russian Church.

locations.label: Monastic life and death — Sarov, Russia

name: St. Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A Greek elder who spent decades as a confessor near Athens, renowned for his gift of clairvoyance and his joyful, Christ-centred spiritual direction. He was canonized in 2013 and his collected conversations have been read by millions across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Priestly ministry and death — Milesi, near Athens

name: St. Abercius of Hierapolis
title: Bishop, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the late 2nd century, renowned as a missionary and wonder-worker. His famous epitaph, discovered in 1882, is one of the oldest Christian inscriptions and describes his travels to Rome and Mesopotamia proclaiming the faith.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Hierapolis (Pamukkale), Phrygia

name: St. Agafia (Agatha) of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young noblewoman of Sicily martyred under Emperor Decius around 250 AD for refusing to renounce her Christian faith and her vow of virginity. She is venerated as the patron saint of Catania and of Sicily, and is invoked against fire and breast diseases.

name: St. Alexander of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who convened the local synod that first condemned Arianism, then led the Orthodox delegation to the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea in 325 AD alongside his deacon Athanasios. He is venerated for his defense of the full divinity of Christ before it was formally defined.

name: St. Alexios, Man of God
title: Venerable
bio: Born to a noble Roman family, Alexios fled his arranged marriage on his wedding night, lived as a beggar in Edessa for seventeen years, then returned to Rome and lived unknown under the staircase of his own family's house until his death. He is a celebrated model of radical humility and voluntary poverty.

locations.label: Seventeen years as a beggar — Edessa (Sanlıurfa)

name: St. Ambrose of Milan
title: Bishop of Milan
bio: Governor of Milan unexpectedly acclaimed as its bishop by the people in 374 AD while still a catechumen. He became one of the great Latin Fathers, championed orthodoxy against Arianism, penned celebrated hymns still sung today, and boldly confronted the Emperor Theodosius over the Massacre of Thessalonica.

name: St. Anastasia the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr, Deliverer from Potions
bio: A Roman noblewoman who used her wealth to minister to Christians imprisoned under Emperor Diocletian, traveling from prison to prison to care for confessors. She was martyred in Sirmium around 304 AD and is venerated across the Orthodox world with the epithet “Deliverer from Potions” for her healing intercessions.

name: Sts. Andronikos and Athanasia
title: Venerable
bio: A married couple of Antioch who, after the death of their two children, mutually agreed to live in consecrated celibacy. Andronikos became a monk in Egypt; Athanasia, unknown to him, also became a monk disguised as a man. They met again years later, and Andronikos only discovered her identity after her death.

name: St. Antipa of Pergamon
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Pergamon in Asia Minor, mentioned in the Book of Revelation (2:13) as “my faithful witness who was killed among you.” He was martyred under Emperor Domitian, traditionally by being cast into a red-hot bronze bull used for pagan sacrifices. He is invoked for toothaches.

name: St. Apollinaris of Ravenna
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Traditionally a disciple of St. Peter the Apostle, he became the first bishop of Ravenna and was martyred after several exiles for refusing to offer sacrifice to pagan gods. The magnificent Byzantine basilicas of Sant’Apollinare in Classe and Sant’Apollinare Nuovo in Ravenna are dedicated to him.

name: Sts. Aquila and Priscilla
title: Apostles
bio: Jewish Christian tentmakers mentioned repeatedly in the New Testament as close companions of St. Paul the Apostle, who worked alongside him in Corinth and Ephesus. They hosted a church in their home and personally instructed the eloquent Apollos in the Christian faith.

name: St. Arsenios the Great
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A highly educated Roman deacon who served as tutor to the imperial princes Arcadius and Honorius in Constantinople, then at the age of forty renounced everything and became a monk in the Egyptian desert. He is remembered for his maxim: “I have often repented of having spoken, but never of having been silent.”

name: St. Athanasios of Athos
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Great Lavra, the oldest and most prestigious monastery on Mount Athos, established in 963 AD with the patronage of Emperor Nikephoros Phokas. He organized cenobitic monastic life on the Holy Mountain and shaped Athonite monasticism for centuries to come.

locations.label: Foundation of the Great Lavra — Mount Athos

name: St. Barbara the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: Daughter of a wealthy pagan of Nicomedia who was locked in a tower by her father to keep her from suitors, she secretly embraced Christianity and had a third window added to her bathhouse in honor of the Trinity. She was tortured and beheaded by her own father after refusing to renounce her faith.

name: St. Blaise of Sebaste
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Sebaste in Armenia and a physician who was said to heal both people and wild animals, he withdrew to a cave during a persecution where he continued his healing ministry. He was arrested, tortured with iron combs, and beheaded, and is invoked to this day against ailments of the throat.

name: St. Boniface of Tarsus
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman servant of dissolute life who was sent by his mistress Aglaida to collect the relics of martyrs in the East, he was so moved by witnessing their courage under torture in Tarsus that he confessed Christ himself and was executed. His own relics were then brought back to Rome by the astonished servants who had accompanied him.

name: St. Charalambos
title: Hieromartyr
bio: An elderly bishop of Magnesia who, at over a hundred years old, was seized during the persecutions of Septimius Severus for continuing to preach Christ. He endured his flesh being flayed with iron hooks without complaint, converting the very soldiers and governor sent to torment him.

name: St. Christina the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Tyre who smashed her father's golden idols and distributed the metal to the poor, she was subjected by him and later by Roman governors to a horrific series of tortures, including being thrown into the sea, all of which she miraculously survived before her eventual martyrdom.

name: St. Clement of Rome
title: Hieromartyr, Pope of Rome
bio: A disciple of the Apostles Peter and Paul who became the fourth Bishop of Rome, he authored an epistle to the Corinthians that is among the earliest surviving Christian writings outside the New Testament. Exiled to Crimea for his preaching, he was drowned in the Black Sea with an anchor tied to his neck.

name: Sts. Cyprian and Justina
title: Hieromartyrs
bio: A renowned pagan sorcerer of Antioch hired to ensnare the Christian maiden Justina, Cyprian found his magic powerless against her prayers and, astonished, converted and burned his books of spells before becoming a bishop. He and Justina were later arrested together and beheaded under Diocletian.

name: St. Daniel the Stylite
title: Venerable
bio: Inspired by St. Symeon the Stylite whom he visited as a young monk, Daniel took up the ascetic discipline of pillar-standing near Constantinople, enduring decades of exposure to the elements. Emperors and patriarchs sought his counsel, and he was even ordained a priest atop his own pillar.

name: St. David of Thessaloniki
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who lived for years in the branches of an almond tree outside Thessaloniki as an extreme act of asceticism, praying exposed to sun and frost. He later left his tree to intercede successfully with the Emperor in Constantinople on behalf of his city, before returning to his monastery to die in peace.

name: St. Dionysius the Areopagite
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A judge of the Areopagus court in Athens who was converted by hearing the Apostle Paul's sermon on the “Unknown God”, he became the first bishop of Athens. Tradition holds he later traveled west to preach the Gospel and was martyred in Lutetia (Paris).

name: St. Ephraim the Syrian
title: Venerable
bio: A deacon and prolific hymnographer of Nisibis and later Edessa, he composed hundreds of hymns and homilies in Syriac defending Orthodox teaching against heresy, many of which remain in liturgical use. His Lenten prayer, “O Lord and Master of my life,” is recited throughout Great Lent in Orthodox churches.

name: St. Eugenia of Rome
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of a Roman prefect of Egypt, she disguised herself as a man to enter a monastery near Alexandria, eventually being chosen as its abbot without her true identity being known. She was later falsely accused, revealed her identity to clear herself, and was ultimately martyred in Rome under Valerian.

name: St. Eustathios Placidas
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman general known as Placidas who converted to Christianity after seeing a vision of Christ between the antlers of a stag while hunting, taking the name Eustathios at baptism. After enduring the loss of his family and fortune as trials of faith, he was ultimately martyred with his wife and sons by being roasted alive in a bronze bull.

name: St. Euthymios the Great
title: Venerable
bio: Born in Melitene in Armenia, he journeyed to the Judean Desert and founded a renowned lavra that became a center of monastic and doctrinal formation, playing a key role in defending Orthodoxy at the Council of Chalcedon. He is honored as one of the great founders of Palestinian monasticism.

locations.label: Foundation of his Lavra — Judean Desert

name: St. Fanourios the Newly-Revealed
title: Great Martyr
bio: Known only from an icon discovered amid the ruins of an ancient church during the excavation of the city walls of Rhodes, depicting scenes of his martyrdom alongside his name, with no other historical record surviving. Devotion to him spread quickly, and to this day the faithful bake “fanouropita” cakes in his honor when seeking help to find lost things.
